## 2. Constructing the receiving operation

Alice prepares
\[
|\Phi_X\rangle_{AS}
=\frac{|0\rangle_A|+\rangle_S+|1\rangle_A|-\rangle_S}{\sqrt2}.
\]
This takes a local memory, a single-qubit preparation, and a local entangling gate. During emission, the source follows its fixed generator. Alice retains \(A\); the final \(S\) is discarded.

Bob uses an \(N\)-level ladder, initially in \(|0\rangle\), with
\[
a_{N-1}=\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}\sqrt j\,|j-1\rangle\langle j|,
\qquad
R(t)=r(t)a_{N-1}.
\]
The accessible and inaccessible source couplings are
\[
C=\sqrt{\eta\gamma}\,Z,\qquad
L_{\rm lost}=\sqrt{(1-\eta)\gamma}\,Z.
\]
The actual forward cascade has Hamiltonian and jumps
\[
H=H_S+\frac{R^\dagger C-C^\dagger R}{2i},
\qquad J_1=C+R,\quad J_2=L_{\rm lost}.
\]
The cross Hamiltonian is supplied by the cascade itself. It is not a direct gate between distant systems. This is the series-product construction of Gough and James, Definition 5.3 and Theorem 5.5. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"}
